title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: The base snapshot (lines 57-67) contains an authorization bypass vulnerability where chaining separate filter() calls on a queryset with related model filters creates multiple joins that can return incorrect results. When filtering `projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)`, Django creates two separate JOIN operations. This allows a project to be returned if: (1) the user is a member of ANY team on the project, AND (2) the project belongs to ANY team with admin access—even if the user is NOT a member of that admin team. The PR fixes this by using Q objects with the & operator (lines 57-71) to combine conditions into a single JOIN, ensuring the filters apply to the same team relationship. The security comment in lines 66-70 of the PR documents this vulnerability.

            # SECURITY: don't chain filters when filtering by related models
            # (query.filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access='admin')),
            # that produces two seprate joins and will return projects where the user is a member,
            # as long as the project belongs to a team with admin access, even if the user is not
            # a member of that team.
            projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(team_filters).exclude(
                organizations__ssointegration__provider=SSOIntegration.PROVIDER_ALLAUTH,
            )

Team types: Admin -- Team members have full access to administer the projects assigned to the team. Read Only -- Team members are only able to read the documentation of each project, and not able to change anything about each project.

findings.suggested_fix: Use Q objects with & operators to combine filters on related models into a single condition, ensuring all filter conditions apply to the same relationship join. This is what the PR implements: `team_filters = Q(teams__members=user)` then `team_filters &= Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)` instead of chaining separate filter() calls.

## Analysis Summary

The PR makes a **critical authorization fix** to the `AdminPermissionBase.projects()` method in `readthedocs/core/permissions.py`:

### The Problem (Base Code)
The base code uses **chained filter calls**:
```python
projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(teams__members=user)
if admin and not member:
    projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)
```

This creates **two separate SQL joins** on the `teams` table. This is a critical authorization bug because:
- The first filter finds all projects where the user is a team member (ANY team)
- The second filter finds all projects that have a team with ADMIN_ACCESS (ANY team)
- The AND combines these with a JOIN, but Django's ORM allows matches where these refer to DIFFERENT team instances
- **Result:** A user is returned projects where they're a member of ANY team AND a different admin team exists on the project - even if they're NOT on the admin team

### The Fix (PR Code)
The PR combines filters using Q objects with `&=` before querying:
```python
team_filters = Q(teams__members=user)
if admin and not member:
    team_filters &= Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)
projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(team_filters).exclude(...)
```

The security comment explicitly documents this:
> "don't chain filters when filtering by related models...that produces two separate joins and will return projects where the user is a member, as long as the project belongs to a team with admin access, even if the user is not a member of that team."

Organizations
-------------

.. include:: /shared/admonition-rtd-business.rst

In this article, we explain how the *organizations* feature allows you to manage access to your projects.
On |com_brand|, your account is linked to an *organization*.
Organizations allow you to define both individual and team permissions for your projects.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`/guides/manage-read-the-docs-teams`
     A step-by-step guide to managing organization owners and teams.

Important objects
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* **Owners** -- Get full access to both view and edit the organization and all projects
* **Members** -- Get access to a subset of the organization projects
* **Teams** -- Where you give members access to a set of projects.

The best way to think about this relationship is:

*Owners* will create *Teams* to assign permissions to all *Members*.

.. warning::

   Owners, Members, and Teams behave differently if you are using
   :ref:`sso_git_provider`.

Team types
~~~~~~~~~~

You can create two types of teams:

* **Admin** -- Team members have full access to administer the projects assigned to the team. Members are allowed to change all of the settings, set notifications, and perform any action under the :guilabel:`Admin` tab for each project.
* **Read Only** -- Team members are only able to read the documentation of each project, and not able to change anything about each project.

Example
~~~~~~~

ACME would set up *Owners* of their organization,
for example, Frank Roadrunner would be an owner.
He has full access to the organization and all projects.

Wile E. Coyote is a contractor,
and will just have access to the new project Road Builder.

Roadrunner would set up a *Team* called *Contractors*.
That team would have *Read Only* access to the *Road Builder* project.
Then he would add *Wile E. Coyote* to the team.
This would give him access to just this one project inside the organization.

Organization owners have full administrative access to the organization and all its projects.

Adding an owner to an organization
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. note::

7. Click :guilabel:`Invite owner`.

The user will receive an invitation and must accept it to become an owner.

Follow these steps:

22:         - projects where the user has access to via VCS SSO.
23:         - Projects where the user has access via Team,
24:           if VCS SSO is not enabled for the organization of that team.
25: 
26:         .. note::
27: 
28:            SSO is taken into consideration,
29:            but isn't implemented in .org yet.
30: 
31:         :param user: user object to filter projects
32:         :type user: django.contrib.admin.models.User
33:         :param bool admin: include projects where the user has admin access to the project
34:         :param bool member: include projects where the user has read access to the project
35:         """
36:         from readthedocs.projects.models import Project
37:         from readthedocs.sso.models import SSOIntegration
38: 
39:         projects = Project.objects.none()
40:         if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
41:             return projects
42: 
43:         if not settings.RTD_ALLOW_ORGANIZATIONS:
44:             # All users are admin and member of a project
45:             # when we aren't using organizations.
46:             return user.projects.all()
47: 
48:         projects_from_sso = Project.objects.none()
49:         projects_from_teams = Project.objects.none()
50:         projects_from_owners = Project.objects.none()
51: 
52:         if admin or member:
53:             # Projects from VCS SSO.
54:             projects_from_sso = cls._get_projects_for_sso_user(user, admin=admin, member=member)
55: 
56:             # Projects from teams that don't have VCS SSO enabled.
57:             team_filters = Q(teams__members=user)
58:             if admin and not member:
59:                 team_filters &= Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)
60:             elif member and not admin:
61:                 team_filters &= Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)
62:             else:
63:                 # If both admin and member are True, we don't need to filter the queryset.
64:                 pass
65: 
66:             # SECURITY: don't chain filters when filtering by related models
67:             # (query.filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access='admin')),
68:             # that produces two seprate joins and will return projects where the user is a member,
69:             # as long as the project belongs to a team with admin access, even if the user is not
70:             # a member of that team.
71:             projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(team_filters).exclude(
72:                 organizations__ssointegration__provider=SSOIntegration.PROVIDER_ALLAUTH,
73:             )
74: 
75:         # Projects from organizations that don't have VCS SSO enabled,
76:         # where the user is an owner.
77:         if admin:
78:             projects_from_owners = Project.objects.filter(organizations__owners=user).exclude(
79:                 organizations__ssointegration__provider=SSOIntegration.PROVIDER_ALLAUTH,
80:             )
81: 
82:         # NOTE: We use a filter with Q objects instead of several union operations
83:         # (e.g projects_from_sso | projects_from_teams | projects_from_owners),
84:         # as the latter can generate a very complex and slow query.
85:         return Project.objects.filter(
86:             Q(id__in=projects_from_sso)
87:             | Q(id__in=projects_from_teams)
88:             | Q(id__in=projects_from_owners)
89:         )
